catalog_quote: 4.2. THE STRESS RULE. I start with a descriptive statement of the stress rule. (12) a. Final syllable is stressed if it contains a long vowel with a coda; b. else penult is stressed if it contains a long vowel; c. else antepenult is stressed. Using the investigated data, the success of the stress rule is 90.4%.10 ... 10. Nathan's (1973a) and Hughes' (2020:138) stress rule, “final if closed else penult,” has a 68% success rate on the same data with the same assumptions about intonation. ... An addendum to the clause (12b) of the stress rule is that closed penultimate syllables also attract stress. The only word-medial codas are first halves of geminate consonants. The effect of the geminate can only be seen where the vowel in the penult is short (16a). sources.quote: 'Although Nauruan stress has been described in fairly simple terms (Nathan, 1973), there is no general agreement about stress patterns in the literature.' Summarizes Nathan's rules: '1. Stress penultimate with final open syllables. 2. Stress final with most (but not all) final closed syllables. 3. Stress initial with reduplications (most of which are frozen).' and Kayser's rules: '1. Stress first syllable of dissyllabic words. 2. For words with more than two syllables, stress the penult if it is long, or the antepenult if the penult is short. 3. For derived words, always stress the suffix. ...
sources.note: Only other Glottolog 'phonology' reference; its stress section (pp. 61-62) relays Kayser 1936's 'penult if long, else antepenult' rule, an independent early witness for the weight-sensitive three-syllable window our record codes from Blumenfeld 2022.

tone.quote: Der dynamisch betonte Vokal wird mit einem ′ versehen. Eine Regel ist für die Akzentuierung noch nicht auffindbar. ... Ton. Der dynamische Akzent ist nicht so ausgeprägt, wie wir es bei den Gruppen der indogermanischen Sprachfamilie gewohnt sind. Dieselben Wörter werden oft verschieden betont. Im großen und ganzen werden alle Silben gleichmäßig betont. In den Texten sind die Silben, bei denen ich einen Hauptton im Worte feststellen konnte, mit dem Schwerezeichen ` versehen worden.
tone.locator: p. 2 (I. Orthographie, transcription signs) and p. 20 (II. Grammatik, 'Zur Lautlehre', paragraph 'Ton.')
tone.translation: The dynamically stressed vowel is marked with ′. A rule for the accentuation cannot yet be found. ... Accent. The dynamic accent is not as pronounced as we are used to from the groups of the Indo-European language family. The same words are often stressed differently. On the whole all syllables are stressed evenly. In the texts, the syllables on which I could detect a main stress within the word have been marked with the grave sign.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: No tones described. Word accent characterised as a weak, variable dynamic (stress) accent with no discoverable rule; syllables said to be roughly evenly stressed; main stress marked ad hoc in the texts with a grave sign.

tone.quote: Nauruan stress is realized primarily as relative differences in F0 across the final two syllables in a given prosodic word. As described in §3.2.3, stress placement is determined by syllable weight, with word-final stress occurring where there is a final heavy syllable and penultimate stress occurring otherwise. ... Nauruan generally aligns stress and high pitch, as do Kosraean and Marshallese; but in other Micronesian languages, such as Kiribati and Pohnpeian, stress and pitch are independent.
tone.summary: Pitch treated only as the main acoustic correlate of weight-based stress (high F0 on the stressed syllable, from spectrograms); no statement on whether Nauruan has lexical tone; phrasal H/L labels.
